newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae to buy stake in Carver.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae to buy stake in Carver.

text.p: Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) has deposited $250,000 in Carver Federal Savings Bank as part of a community development initiative, and will take an equity position, Carver said Tuesday.
A spokesman for Carver, the largest black-owned financial institution in the U.S., when asked for details of the equity stake, said "it is not something we can announce or discuss at the moment."

The $250,000 deposit is part of Fannie Mae's Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFI) initiative, a $25 million commitment to invest in community-based financial institutions. According to a news release from Carver, the investment focus is on community banks based in areas underserved by "majority" institutions.

"We are confident Fannie Mae's investment in Carver Federal will expand financial capacity in Harlem," said James Johnson, chairman and chief executive of Fannie Mae in a statement. "We look forward to working with the bank to increase the number of minority homeowners in the area."

Carver said a Fannie Mae representative will work to enhance the thrift's marketing to potential homeowners. Fannie Mae will also help Carver develop a strategy to become a $1 billion institution by the year 2000. As of June 30, Carver had assets of $363 million.
Carver Federal will also participate in Fannie Mae's mentor program, which matches smaller financial institutions with majority institutions to augment loan production.
"The support of Fannie Mae heightens our visibility as a mainstay in the community development arena," said Thomas Clark, president and chief executive of Carver.
In August, Carver rebuffed a takeover overture from Joseph Curry, a former employee of Bear Stearns Cos Inc.
Carver was up 3/4 to 8-1/2 in morning trade.
